parts.problemMd: Work out the size of one interior angle of a regular 16-sided polygon.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

> *Exterior angles** of a polygon sum to *$360^{\circ}$*.*

> *Divide 360 by 16 to find the size of one **exterior** angle. *

> $360\div16=22.5$* *

> *The **exterior angle **and the **interior angle **of a polygon add up to *$180^{\circ}$*.*

> *Subtract the **exterior** angle from 180 to find the size of the **interior** angle. *

$180-22.5=157.5$

* ***[1]**

$157.5^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *The sum of interior angles = 180° × **(*$n-2$*) because a polygon can be split into *$n-2$* triangles. *

`| Sum of interior angles | = 180 x ( 16 - 2 ) | | _ _ _ | _ = 180 x 14 | | _ _ _ | _ = 2520 |`

> *Divide 2520 by 16 to find the size of one **interior **angle. *

$2520\div16=157.5$

* ***[1]**

$157.5^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

$\frac{180 \left(n - 2\right)}{n}$

$\frac{360}{n}$

$180-\frac{360}{n}$

**[A1]**

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
**Without using a calculator**, work out $1\frac{3}{4}-\frac{11}{12}.$

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Convert *$1\frac{3}{4}$* into an improper fraction by multiplying the whole number by the denominator and adding the numerator.*

> * *

$1\frac{3}{4}=\frac{7}{4}$

* ***[1]**

> *Find an equivalent fraction for *$\frac{7}{4}$* that will give a denominator of 12 (to make both fractions have a common denominator).*

> * *

$\frac{7\times3}{4\times3}=\frac{21}{12}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the fractions.*

> * *

$\frac{21}{12}-\frac{11}{12}=\frac{10}{12}$

> * *

> *Simplify by dividing the numerator (top of the fraction) and the denominator (bottom of the fraction) by 2.*

> * *

$\frac{10\div2}{12\div2}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\frac{5}{6}$** [1]**

parts.problemMd:

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal*

> *The reciprocal of *$\frac{4}{7}$* is *

$1\div\frac{4}{7}=\frac{7}{4}$

> *Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal calculated*

$\frac{15}{28}\times\frac{7}{4}$

**[1]**

$=\frac{15\times7}{28\times4}$

$=\frac{105}{112}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify the fraction by cancelling 7 from both the numerator and the denominator*

$\frac{105}{112}=\frac{7\times15}{7\times16}=\frac{15}{16}$

$\frac{15}{16}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
**Without using your calculator**, work out $1\frac{7}{12}+\frac{13}{20}$

You must show all your working and give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Convert the first fraction so that it is an improper fraction*

$1\frac{7}{12}=\frac{12\times1+7}{12}=\frac{19}{12}$

> *The lowest common multiple of *$12$* and *$20$* can be found by listing the first few multiples*

*Multiples of *$12:12,24,36,48,60...$

*Multiples of *$20:20,40,60...$

> *The lowest common multiple of *$12$* and *$20$* is *$60$

> *Find the equivalent fraction to *$\frac{19}{12}$* with the denominator of *$60$*, by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 5 *

> * *$\frac{19\times5}{12\times5}=\frac{95}{60}$* *

> *Find the equivalent fraction to *$\frac{13}{20}$* with the denominator of *$60$*, by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 3*

$\frac{13\times3}{20\times3}=\frac{39}{60}$

**[1]**

> *Now that both fractions have a common denominator, add the two fractions together*

$\frac{95}{60}+\frac{39}{60}$

**[1]**

$=\frac{95+39}{60}$

$=\frac{134}{60}$

> *Convert the fraction back to a mixed number*

$\frac{134}{60}=\frac{120}{60}+\frac{14}{60}$

$=2\frac{14}{60}$

> *Simplify the fraction fully by dividing the numerator and denominator by 2*

$2\frac{7}{30}$** [1]**

parts.problemMd:

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To multiply fractions, convert the mixed number to an improper (top heavy) fraction.*

$1\frac{1}{7}=\frac{8}{7}$

> *The calculation is now*

$\frac{5}{16}\times\frac{8}{7}$

**[1]**

> *The 16 and the 8 can be cancelled before multiplying to make the next step easier. Rewrite them as products of 8.*

$\frac{5}{8 \\times 2} \\times \frac{8 \\times 1}{7} = \frac{5}{ \cancel{8} \\times 2} \\times \frac{ \cancel{8} \\times 1}{7} = \frac{5}{2} \\times \frac{1}{7}$

> *Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together*

$\frac{5\times1}{2\times7}=\frac{5}{14}$

> *There is no more cancelling that can be done*

$\frac{5}{14}$* ***[1]**

On any Saturday, the probability that Arun plays football is $\frac{3}{4}.$

On any Saturday, the probability that Bob plays football is $\frac{2}{5}.$

parts.solutionMd:
> *The probabilities of all possible outcomes of an event add up to 1.*

> *The probability that Arun plays football on a Saturday is *$\frac{3}{4}$*, the only other option for Arun is that he does not play football. *

> *The probability that Bob plays football on a Saturday is *$\frac{2}{5}$*, the only other option for Bob is that he does not play football. *
*To find the probability that Bob does not play, subtract the probability that he does plays from 1.*

> *The probability that Bob plays is not affected by whether or not Arun plays football.*
